Definition: Integration of voter registration data for identity verification, demographic analysis, and service delivery targeting
Comments: No documented integration of electoral register with InfoHighway or any data exchange platform. Electoral Commission of Mauritius manages voter registration independently. Score 2: planned (within the general interoperability ambition of the Blueprint).
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original Comments asserted a parenthetical 'Score 2: planned' despite the recorded Value Code being 0 (Unknown) - an internal inconsistency in the source row. Checked the InfoHighway official leaflet, which lists the platform's key connected Publisher agencies (Central Business Registration Department, Civil Status Division, Economic Development Board, Mauritius Revenue Authority, National Transport Authority) with no mention of the Electoral Commission, and the Office of the Electoral Commissioner's own site (electoral.govmu.org), which shows it publishes and manages the voter register independently online. No authoritative source states any integration status (current, planned, or explicitly absent) for the electoral register with InfoHighway or any other exchange platform. Confirmed at 0 (Unknown) rather than upgrading to 2 (Planned), since the Blueprint's general interoperability language does not name the Electoral Commission specifically and is too vague to support a score change.
revised_comments: No evidence has been found of integration between Mauritius's electoral register and the InfoHighway government data exchange platform or any other data exchange system. The Office of the Electoral Commissioner maintains and publishes the voter register independently through its own website, with no documented data-sharing link to InfoHighway, whose publicly listed Publisher agencies include the Central Business Registration Department, Civil Status Division, Economic Development Board, Mauritius Revenue Authority and National Transport Authority.

Definition: Level of public transparency regarding data exchange operations, governance, and data sharing agreements
Comments: Mauritius has a Data Protection Office (established under DPA 2017), National Open Data Policy (2017), and a dedicated e-services portal. InfoHighway operates with an InfoWatch dashboard for constant monitoring. The CSEA case study documents impact metrics. Annual reports and governance structures are in place. Blueprint 2025-2029 includes a 'national data governance framework to empower citizens, improve service delivery and embed data-driven decision making'. Score 3: moderate/annual reports with some public dashboard elements.
redteam_note: Value Name differs from the scale label — usually cosmetic.
revision_notes: Fetched ih.govmu.org directly: the public-facing InfoHighway homepage displays a live 'InfoFactsheet' with real-time statistics (33 publishers, 192 connections, 628 e-services, current and previous month query counts, cumulative total queries, and years of administrative working time saved since January 2017), accessible without login. This is a genuine public dashboard rather than only an annual-reporting mechanism, matching the scale's top band ('4=High = Public Dashboard & Reports') more closely than the original 'Moderate/Annual Reports' (3). Re-checked original sources (ih.govmu.org, CSEA case study, Blueprint 2025), which corroborate but do not by themselves establish the dashboard's public accessibility - this was confirmed by directly viewing the live page. No standalone annual transparency report was located, but the continuously live dashboard constitutes stronger and more frequent public disclosure than 'annual reports' implies. Score revised upward from 3 to 4.
revised_comments: Mauritius operates a live public transparency mechanism for its InfoHighway government data exchange: the platform's public-facing homepage publishes a continuously updated 'InfoFactsheet' showing real-time statistics, including the number of publisher agencies, active connections, e-services, monthly and cumulative query volumes, and estimated administrative time saved since January 2017. This sits alongside a Data Protection Office established under the Data Protection Act 2017, a National Open Data Policy (2017), and governance oversight through a High-Level Management Team chaired by the Ministry of Information Technology, Communication and Innovation. An independent case study (CSEA, 2024) documents the platform's impact metrics. This combination of a live public dashboard and supporting governance reporting represents a high level of public transparency regarding data exchange operations.

Definition: Whether data exchange infrastructure and services reach rural and remote areas or concentrate in urban centers
Comments: Mauritius is a small island (~2,040 km2) with relatively high connectivity. Internet penetration is high. The Blueprint 2025-2029 explicitly targets equitable digital access. ITU positions Mauritius as 3rd in Africa for digital infrastructure development. Rural-urban divide is less pronounced than in continental countries. Score 3: equitable urban-rural coverage largely achieved for a small island state.
redteam_note: Value Name differs from the scale label — usually cosmetic.
revision_notes: Confirmed via Statistics Mauritius / Mauritius Digital Promotion Agency ICT indicators: national household internet access rose to 85.8% in the most recent reported year, up from 75.0% at the 2022 housing census and 31.7% in 2011, and the ITU ICT Development Index score for Mauritius was 86.3 in 2023, among the highest in Africa. Mauritius's small land area (~2,040 km2) and integrated national network mean rural/urban infrastructure gaps are much smaller than in continental African states. An academic case study on rural Mauritius (Devi & Ramkumar, 2025) found internet access itself has improved substantially in rural areas, though gaps remain in digital literacy and usage patterns, particularly for women and younger residents - this concerns usage/skills rather than infrastructure/service reach, so does not contradict the infrastructure-focused score. Score of 3 (Equitable Urban-Rural Coverage) confirmed; original Year (2025) revised to 2024 to match the vintage of the underlying ICT indicator and census data actually cited.
revised_comments: Mauritius has achieved largely equitable urban-rural coverage of digital infrastructure and services. National household internet access reached 85.8% in the most recent Statistics Mauritius / Mauritius Digital Promotion Agency ICT indicators, up from 75.0% at the 2022 housing census and 31.7% in 2011, and the ITU rated Mauritius's ICT Development Index at 86.3 in 2023, among the highest scores in Africa. Given the country's small land area of around 2,040 km2 and its integrated national fibre and mobile network, the rural-urban infrastructure divide is markedly smaller than in continental African states, and the Digital Transformation Blueprint 2025-2029 explicitly targets continued equity in digital access, including for the outer island of Rodrigues.
